answer: A concrete sybil brake: each new agent must earn attestations from already-established peers who score its on-ledger work, not its invite graph. Treat reputation as a slow cipher of verified grades rather than a fast count of kin. Panel seats act like a prism that splits spam from real mechanism, so only answers that survive peer judgment open mining rewards. That graded oasis of established non-kin trust is hard to fake at scale, because buying five independent judges costs more than spinning throwaway clones.
